title: 14 times in 10 months, two Election Commissioners objected on record to poll panel steps
shows: From internal notes and letters of October 2025 to August 2026, shows that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi objected on record at least 14 times to SIR decisions, including the Form 6 change, centralised control of the roll software and the West Bengal appeals.

title: 'Illegal, unauthorised': Election Commissioners objected to Form 6 change
shows: Companion piece showing how a new declaration section was added to Form 6 against the written advice of two Commissioners, who said it needed an amendment to the Registration of Electors Rules.

title: 'Differing views' part of 'decision-making', says EC, does not address concerns two ECs red-flagged
shows: Reports the Election Commission's first response to the investigation: it calls the 14 notes suggestions and says every decision was unanimous, and the paper sets out what the response does not address.

title: SIR draft rolls see over 13 crore deletions so far, Delhi leads with 33% left out
shows: Tallies the names left off the draft rolls across the states revised so far, over 13 crore, with Delhi the highest at about a third of its roll.

title: Press Note: Special Intensive Revision - Phase III (No. ECI/PN/086/2026)
outlet: Election Commission of India (copy hosted by the Government of Meghalaya)
shows: The Commission's own announcement of the third phase in 16 states and 3 union territories, with its count of booth level officers and agents and its summary of the first two phases.

title: Bihar SIR: Latest ECI data raises more questions over higher deletions among women
authors: Areena Arora, Srinivasan Ramani, Vignesh Radhakrishnan
shows: Using the list of about 65 lakh deleted Bihar electors the Supreme Court made the Commission publish, shows women far outnumbered men among those marked 'permanently shifted', most of all below age 40.

title: Watch: Bihar SIR: The mystery behind 7 lakh more women elector deletions | Data Point
shows: The Hindu's data team sets the gender gap in Bihar's deletions against census migration records and the age of those removed.

title: More women deleted from rolls in most States after SIR
shows: Compares women per 1,000 men on the 2024 Lok Sabha rolls and the final SIR rolls across the second-phase states and finds the ratio fell in every major state except Tamil Nadu.

title: Why exclusion of women voters in Bihar should worry Nitish Kumar
shows: Compares Bihar's January 2025 roll with the final SIR roll and finds women were close to 59% of the names removed and the gender ratio of the roll fell in 230 of 243 seats.

title: What Election Commission data says about 'vote chori' in the Bihar elections
shows: Checks booth-level results in high-deletion villages, the 28 close contests and late additions to the roll, and finds no anomaly that stands out: the NDA won exactly half the close contests.

title: More men die in Bihar, but more women vanish from its voter rolls
shows: Sets the Commission's deletions by reason and sex against state death records and finds about 7.6 lakh more women than men removed, including more women entered as dead, although more men die.

title: 4 tests, 1 question: Did SIR shape Bengal outcome?
shows: Runs four tests of West Bengal's deletions against 2026 margins and swings: net deletions exceeded the BJP's margin in 82 seats, but exceeded the swing in margin in only 12 flipped seats, and under-adjudication deletions passed the two tests in 49 and 14 seats.

title: Over 61 Lakh Women Dropped from Bengal Voter Rolls, Data Show Stark Gender Bias in SIR
authors: Sabir Ahamed, Ashin Chakraborty, Bhanupriya Rao, Souptik Halder
shows: From the Commission's deletion lists, finds roughly three in five electors removed from or held under adjudication on West Bengal's roll were women, most heavily in Muslim-majority, Scheduled Tribe and Matua seats.

title: SIR exclusions in West Bengal were connected to the AITC lead and Muslim population
shows: Using Sabar Institute deletion data, reports deletions exceeded the margin in 102 of the BJP's 207 seats and, by its own summary, a regression in which deletions rose with how hard a seat was for the BJP to win.

title: SIR and the BJP's Bengal Majority
shows: An economist's counterfactual: even if every adjudicated deletion had voted for the runner-up the BJP keeps a majority, and only under assumptions the data do not support do the wider deletions overturn it.

title: How the Invisible Maths of Electoral Roll Revision Altered West Bengal's Election
shows: An arithmetic sensitivity analysis: gross deletions exceeded the winning margin in 160 seats, and of two no-SIR scenarios one returns the TMC and the other leaves the BJP with a smaller majority. It does not model voter preference.

title: Bengal Has 62 Lakh 'Under Adjudication' Electors. Here's Why That Number Is Significant.
shows: Sets West Bengal's final roll against the National Commission on Population's projection of adults for 2026 and finds a gap of about 65.7 lakh, with electors at about 91.5% of projected adults.

title: Bihar 2025: In 11 Seats, SIR Deletions Outnumbered Victory Margins
shows: Finds 11 Bihar seats where deletions exceeded the winning margin, separates the 47 lakh net fall from the 3.66 lakh removed after the draft, and says the landslide made the numbers moot statewide.

title: 'SIR Risks Disenfranchising Millions of Legitimate Citizens Over Lack of Documents': Lokniti-CSDS Survey
shows: Reports a Lokniti-CSDS survey across Delhi and five states: 52% of respondents had no birth certificate and 41% no domicile certificate, with sharp gaps between states.

title: How ECI's dubious software branded 3.66 crore voters in West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh as suspects
shows: From the Commission's own suspect-list summaries, shows software flagged about 1.31 crore West Bengal and 2.35 crore Madhya Pradesh electors for 'logical discrepancies' with no written protocol for resolving them.

title: ECI misled the Supreme Court on SIR in West Bengal
shows: Uses official records and interviews with election officials to argue the West Bengal notices were produced in bulk by central algorithms, not reviewed one by one by registration officers as the Commission told the Court.

title: Delhi SIR: With More Than Half the Voters in India's Capital Either Purged or on ECI's Doubtful List, VIPs Get a Pass and the Poorest Pay
authors: Shubhangi Derhgawen, Dikshya Koirala, Sumedha Mittal
shows: From booth-wise deletion lists and ground reporting, finds 79.2 lakh of Delhi's 1.45 crore electors were removed or sent a notice, with the heaviest losses among the poorest, including residents of demolished settlements.

title: विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण: वोटर लिस्ट की सफ़ाई के वादे पर वोट देने के मूल अधिकार की कब्र खोदने का इंतज़ाम
authors: The Reporters' Collective (produced by Alok Rajput, per its newsletter of 5 March 2026)
shows: A Hindi video version of the Collective's Electoral Roll Project findings. The date is the newsletter that announced it; the upload date was not confirmed.

title: Supreme Court Upholds Election Commission's Power To Conduct SIR Of Electoral Rolls
shows: Reports the Supreme Court judgment in ADR v. Election Commission holding the SIR within the Commission's powers and its procedure lawful, with a nexus to free and fair elections.

title: Is ECI Correct In Saying Supreme Court Upheld Its New Form 6 Declaration?
shows: Examines whether the May 2026 judgment actually considered the declaration the Commission later added to Form 6, as the Commission claimed.

title: Analysis and Explainer on How the SIR Excluded Voters at Scale
shows: Draws on official deletion figures and an RTI reply on West Bengal appeals: Delhi's draft excluded 32.78% of electors, 91.13% of decided West Bengal appeals restored the elector, and the public still cannot check the rolls.
